beta_new: Jam a finger crack and then a hand crack angling up and right, grunt through the offwidth, then chimney up onto a terrace.

moves.from: Walk off by scrambling third-class ledges leftward down to the rappel anchors.

beta_new: Start where the ramp begins, a little beyond a large tree. Muscle up the overhanging eighty-foot wall past six bolts to a final dyno at the anchors. A medium cam in the crack at mid-height adds extra comfort.

moves.from: A medium cam in the crack at mid-height adds extra comfort.

value.text: A medium cam for the crack at mid-height.

beta_new: Climb past a bolt on moderate rock, then trace a water groove with one bolt to anchors. For the second pitch, take the steeper line of six bolts to the summit anchors.
Begin at the anchor below the large pine and follow the continuous crack, widening from fingers to hands, straight up along the slab's left margin.

The first pitch follows a thin ramp that leans right to a belay with a two-bolt anchor. It is the harder-to-protect section, so small wires matter.

On the second pitch, shift right and jam a brief, fingery crack, the crux, to a comfortable shelf with a two-bolt rappel anchor.

moves.from: small wires matter

value.text: Small wires for the first pitch.

beta_new: A sustained thin face. Start just left of its neighbor and angle rightward through five bolts to the pair of anchor bolts. An alternate start undercling the thin arch farther left.
A crack in the 5.8 range leads to a roof, with the headwall higher up protected by three bolts.

moves.from: Take medium cams for the crack.

value.text: Medium cams for the crack.

beta_new: Start as for the neighboring Renaissance line, clipping a pair of bolts to reach a crack that bends leftward.

moves.from: From there you can merge with that route or rappel.
Bring cams up to a number 4.

value.text: Cams up to #4.

beta_new: Start beneath the left end of the prominent roof at the corner, work up the shallow cracks, and carry on to the summit by sharing the finish of the neighboring South Side Classic.

moves.from: Small wired nuts are the gear of choice.

value.text: Small wired nuts.

beta_new: Start to the left of a toppled tree and follow the obvious finger crack.

moves.from: Gear up to two inches handles it.

value.text: Gear up to 2 in.

beta_new: An overhanging crack that opens from finger size to hands.

moves.from: Cams up to three inches suffice.

value.text: Cams up to 3 in.

The first pitch overcomes an overhanging offwidth for forty feet to a perch beside a big tree; you can also reach that perch by scrambling from the left. The second pitch follows a thin crack, then bears left and up across unprotected face climbing for seventy feet to a comfortable belay shelf.

The last pitch is a short crack and face section shared with a neighboring route.

moves.from: Bring some large gear.

value.text: Some large gear.

Begin beside the large trees at the foot of the face. The first pitch works a broad crack up to a stance, continues in the crack and exits a flare into hand-size jams to belay.

The second pitch jams the corner that faces right, traverses under a clear roof and finishes with a superb hand crack to a roomy belay. The third is an awkward offwidth.

moves.from: Bring gear to about 3.5 inches.

value.text: Gear to about 3.5 in.

beta_new:
Scramble up talus beneath the west-side buttress to the foot of the two obvious cracks. The short first pitch works the pair of hand-size cracks, then makes a delicate traverse onto a ledge.

The second pitch climbs a short, broken corner overhead.

moves.from: A rack of cams and nuts is what you need.

value.text: A rack of cams and nuts.

beta_new: Jam the cracks for sixty or seventy feet but resist the leftward escape. You can fight over to a dangling flake, laybacking onto the fractured shelf, or keep going via the flaring slot overhead, the crux, to a large terrace shared with the neighboring East Ridge climb.

moves.from: Cams to a number 4 are useful.

value.text: Cams to #4.

beta_new: Six bolts, then a pair of anchor bolts, trace the arete's left margin where it borders the huge dihedral.

A right-leaning seam passes three bolts and reaches a polished slab beneath the roof; surmount the roof to reach the last bolt and the lowering point. An easier version veers right over the slab to the anchors of the next route. Thin wires and RPs add security around the middle bolts and below the roof.

moves.from: Thin wires and RPs add security around the middle bolts and below the roof.

value.text: Thin wires and RPs for around the middle bolts and below the roof.

beta_new: Start with the same moves as the route beside it, then peel off to the right after clipping the first bolt and go up through six more to a ledge with anchors.

An indirect way into Turnkorner. Take the steep groove just right of the enormous flake propped at the buttress foot, then pick a line between two neighboring routes on a face pitch and belay close to one of them.

Face climb leftward into a lovely narrow crack and jam it to a belay, then work left once more up to the aged bolt beneath Turnkorner's initial crux, then continue up that route.
Start to the right of a tree and work the twin finger cracks to the shelf.

moves.from: Carry nuts plus small and mid-size cams

value.text: Nuts plus small and mid-size cams.

moves.from: then rappel from the anchors

beta_new: Share the opening moves with a neighbor called Confines of Power, then veer right after clipping its fourth bolt. Three more bolts lead up the steep, overhanging face to a permanent anchor.
Angle up and right over slabby stone to a ledge, then cross a band of coarse pegmatite and wander up to the anchors. Thirteen bolts protect the line.

Start from a grassy shelf next to the south-facing dihedral of the lopsided tower. Climb straight up, using wires and RPs for gear until a bolt about forty feet up, then enjoy face climbing past three more bolts to a stance with two cold-shut anchors.

You can rappel from there or carry on directly over the arch above; a pair of mid-to-large cams protects that move.

moves.from: using wires and RPs for gear until a bolt about forty feet up

value.text: Wires and RPs for the start, up to the first bolt.

moves.from: a pair of mid-to-large cams protects that move

value.text: Two mid-to-large cams for the move over the arch.

beta_new: A shady route starting right off the road. The excellent first pitch moves up cracks and flakes briefly, laybacks one flake to a resting point, then follows a finger crack to a two-bolt anchor on a slanting shelf.
Begin beside the rounded arete, to its left, on the north-west wall. Expect more finicky moves on pebbles and a risky top-out, so bring pads.

Double ropes help if you link the route into one pitch, and plenty of slings tame rope drag; your partner should be solid. Start from the western tip of the long ridge, climb the short wall to a summit, and downclimb easy slabs to a notch with a rappel bolt.

Then follow slab to the headwall, follow a narrow crack beside the left arete to a stance beneath the leaning roof, pass the big roof on its left, traverse fifteen feet right and wrestle up the slot to the top.

beta_new: A sustained line up the steep wall to the right of its neighbor. Step up onto a shelf to begin, clip the bolt overhead, and follow thin slanting cracks to a bolt on the upper slab, topping out on the cliff.

moves.from: Carry RPs plus other small crack protection.

value.text: RPs plus other small crack protection.

beta_new: Pitch one is the sustained finger crack over several roofs. Pitch two continues in broader cracks from the ledge's right end, with a roof move near the start.

moves.from: The rack leans toward RPs, small wires and TCUs, plus cams up to three inches.

value.text: RPs, small wires and TCUs, plus cams up to 3 in.

beta_new:
Start roughly thirty feet left of the neighboring Fat-Bottomed Groove, underneath a gap in the roof. Clip a bolt, reach that gap, then power across horizontal holds, using a bolt plus a pin, to a sandy-floored trough, the crux.

Keep going in the trough or shift leftward onto a fine crack ending at a belay ledge, then ease to gentler ground and exit eastward.

moves.from: A number 2.5 cam is the largest piece needed.

value.text: Cams up to #2.5; nothing larger is needed.

beta_new: A slab leads to a crack that cuts over a roof. Pull the roof to a thin crux, then finish on tricky rock. Six bolts lead to the two-bolt anchor.

A pure offwidth, a shame it is not longer. Haul over an overhanging start using several wedged blocks, then grunt up the crack, bending left close to the top to reach an anchor halfway across the face.
Angles up and to the right past three bolts, finishing on easy ground at ledge anchors.

Climb a neighboring route, People's Choice, up to the second belay of that route, after which you shift right to a second pair of anchors. Extend the first bolt with a long sling, and muscle up the steep, pumpy face; nine bolts protect it.

From the Rock of Ages saddle, head east across a loose, rugged slope to the small saddle between Wilson Peak and Gladstone Peak. From there, traverse the south side of the ridge on Class 3 ledges and climb up to the southwest ridge at around 13,550 ft. Follow the ridge, mostly on a faint path just right of the crest, to a false summit at about 13,900 ft. From the false summit, downclimb roughly 50 ft into a notch, then scramble across stacked blocks and ledges through a prominent gash in the ridge and make the final exposed Class 3 moves to the summit. Take your time on the downclimb; it is the most exposed part of the route and is harder to reverse on the way back.

A strenuous, historic line on the tooth's northern aspect. Battle a broad jam crack (the crux), squirm into the chimney about forty feet up, then grunt to the belay atop Tiger's Tooth, where you choose a finish. Protection comes from nuts and fixed pitons.

moves.from: ; carry cams to number 4

value.text: Cams to #4.

beta_new: The opening pitch jams a sustained finger crack for forty feet to a sloping dihedral. From there, either climb the corner and pull the roof above, or take the bolted arete on the left to a two-bolt belay and rappel station.

moves.from: Bring thin gear, TCUs and cams to a number 2.

value.text: Thin gear, TCUs and cams to #2.

beta_new: Climb straight up a steep slab of bucket holds, clipping two bolts, to a third bolt by a quartz dike that angles left, then follow the dike to one more bolt and the cold-shut anchors shared with Village Idiot. Small to medium wires fill any gaps, including a short crack in the dike below the anchors.

moves.from: Small to medium wires fill any gaps, including a short crack in the dike below the anchors.

value.text: Small to medium wires to fill gaps, including a short crack in the dike below the anchors.

beta_new: The line is an overhanging wide crack along the left side of the big recess, reached by way of the dihedrals beneath it. Gear can be awkward to place, but you can get up the crack without needing true off-width technique.

Expect a lieback-and-stem sequence beside the block's right edge, which is harder now that a loose chockstone that once offered a rest has gone. The route mixes face moves, jams, layback and stem sequences, all with excellent protection.
Ascend the crack around the corner for about a dozen feet, stopping beneath a clear ledge. Then step off rightward onto the wall and work past a tiny corner to a ledge from which you can walk off.
